newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight falls to 7.0/5 pct on foreign lending.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight falls to 7.0/5 pct on foreign lending.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 7.00/50 percent from 9.0 percent on Friday as one foreign bank dumped its excess funds on the market, dealers said on Monday.
They said the foreign bank seemed very long and was lending heavily even after 0800 GMT, when most banks have squared up their positions and the market is usually quiet.
The dealers said the market still faced a liquidity crunch and the foreign bank lending was just an aberration.

"The overnight right now does not reflect the market. It is just that this one bank has come in late and has started lending when everyone has squared up," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
He said the overnight was unchanged at 9.0 percent for most of the afternoon.
Other interbank rates earlier in the day were mostly steady as liquidity remained tight despite a rumoured injection of funds by the central bank last Friday.
"There is no new liquidity in the system. So, rates are still there, unchanged," said the head of money dealing at another Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur.
He said there was a rumour of some fund injections by Bank Negara on Friday. "They were said to have lent one-month money through their agents, but there was no confirmation," he said.
Bank Negara Malaysia does not comment on its open market operations.
One-week to three-week money was at 9.0 percent, one-month at 8.4/5 percent and three-month at 8.10/20 percent, all unchanged from Friday.
The overnight was also expected to remain unchanged around 9.0 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed, futures dealers said.
At 0845 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down four points to 92.07, or an implied yield of 7.93 percent.
September contract was up one at 92.40, or 7.60 percent, December was up three at 92.53, or 7.47 percent, and March 1998 was up one at 92.59, or 7.49 percent.
